text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said Slovak firms should create consortia which would concentrate their commercial activities on eastern markets.

- Slovak state-owned telecom monopoly Slovenske Telekomunikacie has proposed a 100 percent tariff increase for phone calls within Slovakia. It has not yet beeen decided whether the hike will come into effect in November or January.
- Some 40,534 cars were sold in Slovakia over the first eight months of this year. The Czech car maker Skoda accounted for about 30.4 percent of the overall figure.

NARODNA OBRODA - Deputy Foreign Minister Jozef Sestak said Slovakia was now reconsidering a Russian proposal to create a free-trade zone. Sestak said Bratislava was consulting with the European Union about the move

- Two other Slovaks were reported to have been kidnapped in Chechnya, bringing the total to three. The first kidnapped Slovak should be released after his Czech employer, the construction company Stavoinform, pay the promised $150,000 ransom.

PRAVDA - The National Property Fund (NPF) on Thursday approved the privatisation of another 30 companies, mostly agricultural firms. The sale does not include the four largest financial institutions slated for privatisation.
- Economics Minister Karol Cesnek said the planned recovery programme for the Slovak engineering industry should increase annual production to around 111 billion crowns in the year 2000.
